# AI usage log (honest record)

**AI tool:** Claude (Anthropic) running as an agent with a shell, file tools and a browser. All code, data generation, tests and documents in this repository were generated by it in one working session. There was no existing code before this Quest; everything is new.

**No AI model runs inside the QA tool.** The dashboard and engine are deterministic Python. "AI-assisted" here means the tool was designed, written, executed and debugged by an AI agent. The tool does not call any AI service.

## What the AI produced

| Area | Output |
|---|---|
| Design | Ablation approach (re-introduce one defect at a time into the corrected engine), ground-truth labels + independent oracle, 8 defect classes. |
| Code | `src/*`, `baseline/faulty_calculator.py`, `app.py`, `tools_mutation_check.py` |
| Data | Seeded generator, labels, manifest, oracle. |
| Tests | 127 pytest tests, subprocess meta-tests, mutation check (9 mutants). |
| Docs | README, intent.md, final-directive.md, reports, Loom script. |

## What the AI got wrong, and how it was corrected (all real events from this session)

1. **Corner-touch test geometry.** The AI wrote a "segment touches a zone corner" test whose segment actually passed through the corner into the interior. The test failed; the AI fixed the geometry (segment now ends exactly on the corner).
2. **Over-tight tolerance.** Tests expected an entry segment to bill exactly 50 % inside. Coordinates stored at 7 decimals (about 1 cm) move the crossing point slightly, giving about 0.3 mm difference. The AI loosened the tolerance to the coordinate precision and documented the reason, instead of weakening the engine.
3. **Helper used outside its valid range.** A clean-trip test ran `road_a()` past the end of ROAD_A's first leg; pings drifted off the road and were (correctly) rejected, so the test failed. Fixed the test data.
4. **Masked defect in a test.** A "noise is billed by the baseline" test used a 400 m offset. That ping also implies about 152 km/h, so the speed rule caught it even with the off-road rule disabled. This turned into a real finding: overlapping rules mask each other, so per-defect (marginal) impacts do not sum to the total. It is stated in the defect report and dashboard. The test now uses a 200 m offset (88 km/h) so only the off-road rule can catch it.
5. **Wrong magnitude assumption.** The same test first demanded +0.5 km; the actual detour is 0.2 km. Threshold corrected to +0.15 km after printing the numbers.
6. **Python/numpy pitfall.** `assert (np.float64 > 0) is True` fails because the result is `np.bool_`; wrapped in `bool()`.
7. **Streamlit test assumptions.** The first AppTest used the wrong selectbox index and an option value instead of its formatted label; fixed by looking the widget up by label. A deprecated `use_container_width` was replaced by `width="stretch"`.
8. **Weak evidence in the first mutation run.** With `-x` the mutation check only showed one early failing dataset test per mutant. It was rerun without `-x` and reports the number of failing tests.

## Alternatives the AI considered and rejected

* Baking per-defect flags into the baseline so that ablation could run on it: rejected because it would duplicate correct logic inside the "faulty" code. Chosen instead: ablation switches on the corrected engine, plus a test proving that all switches off reproduces the baseline to 1e-9 km.
* Using the engine's own filters to produce expected results: rejected (circular). The oracle uses generator ground truth, shapely and different formulas.
* Real map-matching / OSM roads: rejected as out of scope for a 6-10 hour exercise and because it would bring non-synthetic data.

## Verified by execution (not by reading)

Every claim in the reports is backed by a command that was run: dataset size, rejection counts per reason (match the seeded counts exactly), oracle match (max error about 1e-9 km), 127 passing tests, baseline regression failing 2 of 2 and corrected passing 2 of 2, 9 of 9 mutants killed, dashboard smoke test plus a live Streamlit health check (HTTP 200).
